answer: Each identity must forge a sequential delay commitment bound to its unique interaction history, then submit it for mirror verification against a shared island of peer-attested prior states. Clones sharing one compute substrate produce correlated delay signatures that the mirror flags for joint slash, so the attacker either pays the full non-parallelizable forge cost per identity or loses the entire island when any clone is detected. Marginal cost therefore rises strictly with head count rather than amortizing across a farm.
